entities.text: Udathu Suresh, vs The State Of Ap
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.4964 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioner/accused seeks to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.106 of 2019 of Addanki Police Station, registered for the offences under Sections 188, 272 and 420 of IPC and Sections 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act').

2. The allegations against the petitioner briefly are that on 27.03.2019 at 16.30 hours, when the complainant along with his staff conducted a raid on the godown of accused located at Anjaneya Complex, Addanki Town, found the banned tobacco products and under the cover of mediator's report, arrested the accused and registered a case in Crime No.106 of 2019 for the offences stated supra.
3.

Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto basing on the report of the Sub-Inspector of Police of Addanki Rural Police Station.

entities.text: Police of Addanki Rural Police Station
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Therefore,
it is the violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned and therefore,
the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioner under Sections 188, 272 and 420 of IPC and Sections 59 and 63 of FSS Act are hereby quashed.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
